# tenzir_hosted_deployment (Resource)

A deployment that Tenzir runs. The platform starts it and hands it its key, so it needs no install. Creating it waits until the deployment connects, for at most the `create` timeout (15 minutes by default). Destroying it stops and removes it.

Needs `Workspace.createHostedDeployment` and `Deployment.read`, `Deployment.readTracker`, `Deployment.update`, `Deployment.changeTracker`, `Deployment.changeType` and `Deployment.delete`; parents given by slug also need `Workspace.read`. The platform hosts deployments only on Enterprise; `tenzir_deployment_types` says whether it does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "tenzir_deployment_types" "soc" {
  organization_id = data.tenzir_organization.acme.id
  workspace_id    = tenzir_workspace.soc.id
}

resource "tenzir_hosted_deployment" "cloud" {
  organization_id = data.tenzir_organization.acme.id
  workspace_id    = tenzir_workspace.soc.id
  name            = "Cloud"
  size            = data.tenzir_deployment_types.soc.default_size
  region          = data.tenzir_deployment_types.soc.regions[0]

  timeouts {
    create = "20m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The display name. Renaming keeps the deployment's ID and key.
- `organization_id` (String) The ID or slug of the organization.
- `workspace_id` (String) The ID or slug of the workspace the deployment belongs to.

### Optional

- `auto_deploy` (Boolean) Whether new commits on `branch` deploy on their own. Defaults to `true`. When false, the deployment keeps the configuration it has until someone deploys a commit.
- `branch` (String) The branch of the workspace repository whose configuration the deployment runs. Defaults to `main`. The platform refuses to switch to a branch without commits.
- `image` (String) A `tenzir/tenzir` image to run instead of the one the platform hosts deployments with, such as a `reference` from `tenzir_deployment_images`. The platform does not report the image back, so Terraform keeps what it was given: changing it replaces the deployment, and after an import Terraform takes the configured image as given.
- `region` (String) The cloud region it runs in, one of those `tenzir_deployment_types` offers. Defaults to the first. Changing it replaces the deployment.
- `size` (String) The size it runs as, one of those `tenzir_deployment_types` offers. Defaults to the offer's `default_size`. Changing it restarts the deployment; its pipelines resume once it is back.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the deployment was created.
- `id` (String) The deployment ID.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization>/<workspace>/<deployment>, the first two each an ID or a slug.
terraform import tenzir_hosted_deployment.cloud acme/soc/0b3c5d1e-7f8a-4b2c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
```
